reporting.window_note: Each daily run reports year-to-date: Jan 1 -> latest available business date this year, versus the SAME elapsed window last year. The comparison is like-for-like because the model pairs current/last-year values at the row level and the refresh trims last year to the same elapsed day (verified: July exists as days 1-27 in BOTH 2026 and 2025). No month-end wait; the snapshot updates every refresh.
reporting.data_as_of_source: MAX(MIS_DEEP_DIVE2[max_date]) over ALL rows = the latest loaded business date. Key the run off this, NOT the calendar date (data typically runs a few days behind today).
reporting.alignment_guard: The daily job asserts current_elapsed_days == last_year_elapsed_days for the loaded window and flags divergence -- the whole comparison depends on the ETL continuing to trim last year to the same elapsed day.
reporting.bills_caveat: Footfall / ATV / UPT draw bills from CAT_TRANSACTIONS, which has NO date column (monthly grain). Their elapsed alignment cannot be date-verified and is an ETL assumption (current magnitudes look correct). Confirm with the data owner.
reporting.benchmark_note: Thresholds are data-driven bands derived from THIS model's own month-to-month volatility (6 complete months, Jan-Jun 2026 vs 2025). On a smooth cumulative YTD number they act as absolute health lines rather than statistical control limits -- fewer false alarms, which suits a YTD alarm. green_at / amber_at are the machine-evaluable cut points; see evaluate_status().
reporting.evaluation: higher_is_better: green if value>=green_at, else amber if value>=amber_at, else red (severe if severe_at set and value<severe_at).  lower_is_better: green if value<=green_at, else amber if value<=amber_at, else red.

kpis.name: Average Selling Price (ASP) Growth %
kpis.formula: asp_current = rev_current / qty_current; asp_past = rev_past / qty_past; (asp_current - asp_past) / asp_past
kpis.dax:
ASP Growth % =
VAR AspCurrent = [retail price current year]
VAR AspPast = [retail price past year]
RETURN
DIVIDE ( AspCurrent - AspPast, AspPast )

source_measures.rate: NOT materialized as a % anywhere in the model or dashboard — this is a genuinely new measure
source_measures.value: [RETAIL PRICE GROWTH]  (absolute currency delta, already exists — the dax above reuses it)

benchmark_basis.note: Negative every month this year -- basket depth is structurally shrinking. Bands benchmark against this baseline instead of zero, so the alarm fires on deterioration (< -5%), not on the permanent-negative reading (which a green>=0 rule would flag red forever).

source_measures.note: Calls the native measure directly. The local Desktop file's CAT_TABLE identifies a category via CATEGORY_NAME; the published dataset's CAT_TABLE has no such column at all (uses special_product_group_name instead) -- reconstructing this KPI's DISTINCTCOUNT/FILTER logic from raw columns would have to guess which one applies, so it defers to the model's own already-correct [Measure]/[COUNT]/[COUNT_TOTAL] internals instead.
source_measures.scope_note: When scoping to a period, [COUNT] must be filtered via a RELATED table's month (brand table), NOT CAT_TABLE[month]: [Measure] uses ALLEXCEPT(CAT_TABLE, special_product_group_name) which silently wipes a CAT_TABLE[month] filter (returns all-month decline, e.g. 32% instead of the correct 50% for July). For the YTD window this is moot (no month filter), but critical if a period scope is ever added.

kpis.name: At-Risk Revenue Concentration Delta
kpis.formula: share_current = declining_rev_current / total_rev_current; share_past = declining_rev_past / total_rev_past; share_current - share_past
kpis.dax:
At-Risk Revenue Concentration Delta =
VAR ShareCurrent = DIVIDE ( [sum deg cur rev], [sum total cur rev] )
VAR SharePast = DIVIDE ( [sum deg past rev], [sum total past rev] )
RETURN
ShareCurrent - SharePast

source_measures.share_current: [contribution cur]  — already exists, but uses unsafe raw division; the dax above wraps both shares in DIVIDE

benchmark_basis.note: Always deeply negative (declining categories' share of revenue is falling YoY -- good). Bands benchmark against this baseline so the alarm can actually fire when the delta deteriorates toward 0; the old 'red > +3%' line was effectively unreachable.
